_comment: Everything the orchestrator needs to know about this instrument beyond its commands. Delete the sections you do not need. library_types: files it reads (a parameter becomes a picker). result_types: folders under Results/ it writes (created when the server starts, listed on the Results page). parameter_defaults: parameters a workflow may omit. traceability: commands that prepare (prepares_plate) or measure (measures_plate) a plate. resources: what each command physically occupies, so the orchestrator knows what must not run at the same time — READ docs/ADDING_NEW_INSTRUMENT.md before editing that one. See v1/src/catalog.py and v1/src/resources.py.

resources._comment: Delete this section and the orchestrator serialises every step of this instrument against every other instrument that also declares nothing — safe, but nothing of yours will ever overlap with anything. Declaring is how concurrency is earned. provides: the physical things THIS instrument owns. Give an id to anything another instrument can reach into (a deck, a tray, a carousel) so a robot can claim it by name; keep instrument:<key> as the instrument itself. commands: what each command occupies while it runs. Two steps whose claims share an id never run together. control: true marks a command that occupies NOTHING and must run while the instrument is busy — a stop, a pause, a status read. Get this wrong and your abort will queue behind the run it is meant to abort. holds: for a resource that stays occupied AFTER the command finishes, until another command releases it — a plate left in a tray. Only add one if a later step always releases it; validation refuses a workflow where nothing does. by_parameter: use it when what a command occupies depends on an argument rather than on the command (one ExecuteTask that goes to different stations). Full guide and worked examples: docs/ADDING_NEW_INSTRUMENT.md.
